notes: §1985:VII.2.2.2 prints FILE-CONTROL. { file-control-entry } ...: the braces require at least one entry (§1985:IV.2.1.4: 'one of the options contained within the braces must be either explicitly specified or implicitly selected'), then as many as wanted. fileControlParagraph parses the header, its period and fileControlClauseGroup*, BindFileControl binds each entry, and the lower bound the prior PARTIAL read found missing is now enforced: VisitInputOutputSection refuses a paragraph with no entry at 85 (COBOL0900, construct FileControlEntryOptional2002, kb/Work PB5167) and the same source runs at --std 2002. Probed at --std 85: (b) FILE-CONTROL. alone, FILE-CONTROL. then I-O-CONTROL., FILE-CONTROL written twice (COBOL0001), the header without its period (COBOL0307) and an entry without its period before I-O-CONTROL (COBOL0312) are refused; (e) three entries, OPTIONAL relative dynamic with RELATIVE KEY and FILE STATUS, indexed random, and sequential, compile and run, OPEN INPUT of the absent optional file giving 05 and the READ NEXT after it AT END with 10. The witness declares two files and reads both back. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming no kb/Work note; the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5167 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-09.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-09-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985: "FILE-CONTROL. { file-control-entry } …"; 2023: "FILE-CONTROL. [ file-control-entry ] …". 1985 braces require at least one file-control-entry. The 2023 brackets make it optional, so a FILE-CONTROL paragraph with no entries is now accepted.
